verified.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
verified.why: Interleaves reasoning and tool actions in one loop; the basic scaffold pattern that long-running agent loops build on.

verified.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
verified.why: Agents write verbal feedback after failures and retry; a basic verification-and-retry loop for long runs.

verified.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
verified.why: Memory stream of observations, reflection into insights, and retrieval by recency, importance and relevance: a template for multi-day coherence.

verified.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
verified.why: Stores conversation memories with a forgetting curve, so older memories fade while recent or repeatedly used ones persist across many sessions.

verified.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
verified.why: Keeps a growing skill library of verified code so later sessions reuse earlier work; a lifelong-agent memory design.

verified.title: Large Language Models as Tool Makers
verified.why: The LLM writes its own reusable tools in a closed loop and keeps them for later problems, so capability grows without training.

verified.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
verified.why: Shows models miss facts placed mid-context, the core long-context failure agents hit as their history grows.

verified.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
verified.why: Learns from its own past trajectories by extracting insights and examples, then reuses them at inference with frozen weights.

verified.title: Recursively Summarizing Enables Long-Term Dialogue Memory in Large Language Models
verified.why: Recursive summaries keep long dialogue memory usable without re-reading the full history, a basic compaction pattern.

verified.title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
verified.why: Frames agent memory as working, episodic, semantic and procedural stores inside one decision loop, giving a shared vocabulary for long-running agents.

verified.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
verified.why: Token-level prompt compression that shrinks long inputs with small accuracy loss; an early tool for trimming context.

verified.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
verified.why: Real GitHub issues as the standard test for repo-level coding agents; the baseline long coding harnesses are measured against.

verified.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
verified.why: Pages memory between a small context window and external storage, so agents can run past the window limit in long conversations.

verified.title: CLIN: A Continually Learning Language Agent for Rapid Task Adaptation and Generalization
verified.why: Language agent that keeps improving across trials through a memory of causal abstractions, with no fine-tuning.

verified.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
verified.why: Task-agnostic prompt compression distilled from a teacher model; faster and more faithful for trimming agent context.

verified.title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents
verified.why: Early survey that organizes scattered memory mechanisms in LLM agents, a baseline map for long-running agent memory.

verified.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
verified.why: Indexes knowledge as a graph and retrieves associatively, linking facts across many documents for multi-hop recall a long-running agent needs.

verified.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
verified.why: Shows the agent-computer interface (tool design) strongly affects coding-agent results; a core harness design lesson.

verified.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
verified.why: A fixed localize-repair-validate pipeline competes with open agent loops on SWE-bench Lite; a counterpoint on harness complexity.

verified.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
verified.why: Open agent platform with a sandboxed runtime and event-stream history; a concrete harness for long coding runs.

verified.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
verified.why: Compares RAG with long-context LLMs and proposes a hybrid, informing when to retrieve versus keep everything in context.

verified.title: Agent Workflow Memory
verified.why: Induces reusable workflows from past successful trajectories and feeds them into later tasks, so repeated subtasks get cheaper over runs.

verified.title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks
verified.why: An orchestrator keeps a task ledger and tracks progress across specialist agents; a multi-agent coordination pattern.

verified.title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
verified.why: Multi-step workplace tasks with checkpoints that give partial credit; shows long, multi-step tasks remain hard for agents.

verified.title: Lifelong Learning of Large Language Model based Agents: A Roadmap
verified.why: Explains why deployed LLM agents stay static and maps the methods that let them keep learning after deployment.

verified.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
verified.why: Temporal knowledge graph memory that tracks when facts were true and when they were learned, so changed facts update without losing history.

verified.title: Position: Episodic Memory is the Missing Piece for Long-Term LLM Agents
verified.why: Argues long-term LLM agents need episodic memory with five key properties for single-shot, context-specific learning as environments change.

verified.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
verified.why: Builds Zettelkasten-style linked notes that update older memories when new ones arrive, so memory reorganizes itself as history grows.

verified.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
verified.why: Taxonomy of 14 failure modes from annotated multi-agent traces, including premature termination and missing verification.

verified.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
verified.why: Defines the 50% time horizon: how long a task an agent completes half the time; the main measure of long-run ability.

verified.title: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
verified.why: Web agent that explores, abstracts experience into reusable skills and hones them, so later runs call skills instead of re-exploring.

verified.title: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
verified.why: Adaptive memory of reusable solution notes that persists lessons across tasks beyond a single context window.

verified.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
verified.why: Extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient facts from conversations, with a graph variant, targeting consistent memory across long multi-session dialogue.

verified.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
verified.why: Coding agent that rewrites its own code and keeps an archive of variants, a clear case of open-ended self-improvement over runs.

verified.title: Memory OS of AI Agent
verified.why: OS-style memory manager with hierarchical storage for agents, aimed at long-term memory and personalization in long conversations.

verified.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
verified.why: Consolidates memory and reasoning into a compact internal state, keeping agent context small over long tasks.

verified.title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
verified.why: Treats memory as a managed system resource for long-context reasoning, continual personalization and knowledge updates across extended use.

verified.title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
verified.why: Surveys how context is retrieved, processed and managed for LLM systems; a map of the whole theme.

verified.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
verified.why: Evolves prompts by reflecting in language on sampled trajectories, reported to beat RL while needing far fewer rollouts.

verified.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
verified.why: Surveys techniques that let agents improve automatically after deployment, rather than staying fixed as manually configured systems.

verified.title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
verified.why: Adapts agents continually through a case memory the planner reuses, a learning path that avoids fine-tuning the LLM itself.

verified.title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
verified.why: Trains search agents to summarize accumulated context so long-horizon search can continue past context limits.

verified.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
verified.why: Distills reasoning strategies from both successful and failed runs into memory that guides future tasks at test time.

verified.title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
verified.why: Optimizes what a compressor keeps from agent histories across long-horizon tasks, cutting context while protecting success.

verified.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
verified.why: Evolving structured playbook updated by generator, reflector and curator roles to avoid context collapse in long runs.

verified.title: Training-Free Group Relative Policy Optimization
verified.why: Learns experiential knowledge as a token prior, a GRPO-like improvement signal that needs no parameter updates.

verified.title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding
verified.why: Folds finished sub-trajectories into short summaries, letting long-horizon tasks run inside a bounded context.

verified.title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
verified.why: Web agent that proactively manages its own context during long browsing runs instead of waiting for overflow.

verified.title: Context Engineering 2.0: The Context of Context Engineering
verified.why: Position paper on what context engineering is and what context itself must hold in agent systems.

verified.title: Hindsight is 20/20: Building Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects
verified.why: Builds agent memory that retains, recalls and reflects, critiquing top-k snippet retrieval so agents can accumulate experience across sessions.

verified.title: Memory in the Age of AI Agents
verified.why: Recent survey that tries to fix fragmented agent-memory terminology, useful for choosing which memory kinds a long-running agent needs.

verified.title: Recursive Language Models
verified.why: Lets a model call sub-models over a long prompt held outside the window, instead of loading all of it into context.

verified.title: EverMemOS: A Self-Organizing Memory Operating System for Structured Long-Horizon Reasoning
verified.why: Self-organizing memory with an engram-inspired lifecycle that consolidates evolving user states and resolves conflicts for long-running agents.

verified.title: FadeMem: Biologically-Inspired Forgetting for Efficient Agent Memory
verified.why: Adds selective forgetting with adaptive decay, so agents avoid both catastrophic loss at context limits and overload from keeping everything.

verified.title: Graph-based Agent Memory: Taxonomy, Techniques, and Applications
verified.why: Survey of graph-structured agent memory for relational and hierarchical recall in long-horizon tasks, covering techniques and applications.

verified.title: Anatomy of Agentic Memory: Taxonomy and Empirical Analysis of Evaluation and System Limitations
verified.why: Survey plus empirical study finding existing memory benchmarks underscaled, metrics misaligned and system costs overlooked.

verified.title: Is Agent Memory a Database? Rethinking Data Foundations for Long-Term AI Agent Memory
verified.why: Position paper naming failure modes of storage-style agent memory, such as unregulated growth and missing semantic revision, that long-running agents hit.

verified.title: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
verified.why: First systems characterization of how agent memory behaves on long-horizon, stateful workloads, relevant to multi-day agent design.

verified.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search
verified.why: Diagnoses context rot in long-horizon search agents and tests mitigations for it.

verified.title: The Compaction Cliff in Long-Running AI Agent Memory
verified.why: Examines a sharp failure point in long-running agent memory tied to compaction, relevant to multi-day runs.

verified.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
verified.why: Learns when to compact context during long coding runs instead of using a fixed threshold.

verified.title: Self-Evolving Agents Can Repair Failures but Struggle to Generalize from Them
verified.why: Finds agents that learn only from their own failures can repair errors but often struggle to transfer the fix to new tasks.

verified.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
verified.why: Tests whether nonparametric self-evolving agents keep learning new tasks over time without forgetting earlier ones, a direct long-run check.

verified.title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
verified.why: Tests whether agents keep following their rules after compaction, a safety-relevant failure mode for long runs.

verified.title: Length Is Cheap, Competition Is Not: Attention Predicts Context Rot in Retrieval
verified.why: Links attention competition to context rot in retrieval, explaining why accuracy falls as inputs grow.

verified.title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
verified.why: Shows naive cross-task memory can make agents worse than memoryless ones, then proposes expectation-grounded procedural memory to fix it.

verified.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
verified.why: Memory evolves from the agent's own failures without changing weights, tools or workflows, aimed at enterprise agents that keep changing.
